receipts.statement: For an arbitrary law p on subsets S of [n], H_2(p)<=sum_i h_2(q_i), where q_i=P(i in S); this fact alone cannot yield H_2(p)<=C sum_i q_i with universal C.
receipts.proof_or_counterexample: Entropy chain rule and conditioning give subadditivity. For n=1, P(S={1})=q and P(S=empty)=1-q gives H/I=h_2(q)/q>=log_2(1/q), unbounded as q tends to zero. The prior P0162 attempt card also records an n-singleton law obstruction and the Boolean f^2=1 constraint.
receipts.remaining_gap: General probability laws need not be Boolean Fourier spectra; Boolean convolution identities are required for FEI.
receipts.status: independently checked proof for arbitrary laws

receipts.statement: w505's exact identity Delta_i=sum_T r_T[h_2(w_T)+J(t_T)] and nonnegative lower bound by sum_T b_T^2 log_2(r_T/b_T^2) hold for Boolean uniform-cube f.
receipts.proof_or_counterexample: Expanding phi(x)=x log_2(1/x) on each Fourier pair gives the equality; J(t)=1-h_2((1+t)/2)>=0. The binary entropy term r h_2(w) includes b^2 log_2(r/b^2), with a further nonnegative term. Zero r contributes zero.
receipts.remaining_gap: The identity has no universal upper bound by a single coordinate influence; the suitable-coordinate lemma remains unproved.

receipts.statement: For F_m(u,v,y)=(-1)^(u dot v)-(1-y)1{u=v=0}, Delta_y(F_m)/I_y(F_m) >= log_2((2^m-1)^2+1); hence no universal bound Delta_i(f)<=C I_i(f) can hold for every Boolean f and every coordinate i.
assumptions: uniform measure on {0,1}^{2m} times selector y in {-1,1}
receipts.proof_or_counterexample: Independent Walsh derivation gives Bhat(alpha,beta)=2^-m(-1)^(alpha dot beta), dhat=2^-2m, I_y=2^-2m. Entropy identity gives Delta_y=sum_T r_T[h_2(b_T^2/r_T)+J(2a_Tb_T/r_T)] >= I_y log_2((2^m-1)^2+1). Direct truth-table run: python -X utf8 test_selector.py, m=1,2,3 ratios 4.867668747, 8.030013847, 10.255970235; each exceeded its lower bound; total influences matched m+(2m+1)/2^(2m).
receipts.remaining_gap: This refutes only the all-coordinate induction input. A suitable-coordinate or amortized lemma is still unproved; it does not settle FEI.
receipts.status: independently checked proof of intermediate counterexample

receipts.statement: w505's bent-point selector family F_m has H_2(F_m)<=2I(F_m) for every m>=1.
receipts.source_quote: The complete H/I ratio therefore does not grow like the defective Delta_y/I_y ratio.
receipts.proof_or_counterexample: The selector-present spectral slice has mass rho=2^-2m; conditional on selector presence or absence, at most 2^(2m) base Fourier indices occur. Thus H<=2m+h_2(rho). Direct flips give I=m+(2m+1)rho; h_2(rho)<=2m rho+rho/ln2 yields H<=2I. Independent truth tables m=1,2,3 corroborated.
receipts.remaining_gap: Only this family is covered, and FEI for every Boolean function is unproved.
receipts.status: independently checked proof of special family

receipts.statement: For any Boolean f and coordinate i, 0<=Delta_i(f)<=h_2(q)+4q(1-q), q=Inf_i(f).
receipts.proof_or_counterexample: From the exact identity, Jensen gives sum r h_2(w)<=h_2(q); J(t)<=t^2<=4w(1-w), and Jensen on w(1-w) gives sum r J(t)<=4q(1-q). J(t)<=t^2 follows from its positive even-power series whose coefficients sum to J(1)=1.
receipts.remaining_gap: h_2(q)/q diverges as q tends to zero; prior owner memory records a sharper high-influence reduction, so no novelty is asserted.
receipts.status: independently checked proof of elementary bound

receipts.statement: If every nonconstant Boolean f has some relevant i with Delta_i(f)<=K Inf_i(f) for one universal K, then FEI follows with the same K.
assumptions: the universal suitable-coordinate premise is assumed
receipts.source_quote: A sufficient unproved input for full FEI is the existence of a universal C
receipts.proof_or_counterexample: Induction uses exact entropy and influence recursions and the constant-function base case. This duplicates the conditional reduction checked in w504 C002 and the 2026 primary paper's induction framework.
receipts.remaining_gap: The premise is not proved, so the full FEI conjecture does not follow from work in these packets.
